requirement: Set up a complete testing and CI stack for an existing FastAPI service. Use pytest with async fixtures, httpx's ASGI transport for endpoint tests without a live server, pytest-cov with an 80 percent gate, Hypothesis for property-based tests of the validation layer, and ruff for linting. Wire it into GitHub Actions running against a Postgres service container. Use testcontainers-python for the docker container management library.

doc_sources.title: FastAPI – Official Documentation
doc_sources.rationale: The URL https://fastapi.tiangolo.com is the official documentation site for FastAPI, hosted by the framework's author. It is the root landing page for the current version, matching the highest priority criteria.

doc_sources.title: pytest documentation
doc_sources.rationale: The URL is the official documentation site for pytest, hosted at docs.pytest.org, which is the primary entry point for the stable version. It is the root contents page, not a third‑party site. High confidence.

doc_sources.title: HTTPX – A next‑generation HTTP client for Python
doc_sources.rationale: The URL https://www.python-httpx.org is the official documentation site for the Python httpx library, matching the library name and providing a root landing page with docs, installation, and usage. It is the primary source maintained by the library authors, making it the best entry point.

doc_sources.title: pytest-asyncio documentation
doc_sources.rationale: The first result is the library's own Read the Docs site, which serves as the official documentation root for pytest-asyncio. This matches the top priority criteria. The site is current and maintained, making it the best entry point.

doc_sources.title: pytest-cov documentation
doc_sources.rationale: The library provides its own dedicated documentation site on Read the Docs (https://pytest-cov.readthedocs.io), which is the primary entry point for official docs and is more specific than the generic GitHub repo or third‑party tutorials. This matches the top priority of using the library's own docs site.

doc_sources.title: Hypothesis documentation
doc_sources.rationale: The root page on hypothesis.readthedocs.io is the library's own documentation site and serves as the main entry point for users. It is the official docs rather than a deep link or third‑party source. The quickstart page and developer resources are sub‑pages, and the GitHub repo is a fallback if needed.

doc_sources.title: astral-sh/ruff – GitHub
doc_sources.rationale: The official repository for the Python linter Ruff is hosted at github.com/astral-sh/ruff. No dedicated documentation site appears in the provided results, so the repo serves as the primary source of documentation and reference. It is first‑party and current.

doc_sources.title: testcontainers-python documentation
doc_sources.rationale: The library provides its own ReadTheDocs site, which is the primary official documentation host. The root URL redirects to the latest version, making it the best entry point for crawling. All other results are just version‑specific subpaths of the same site.
